corrections.new:
Under the fleet-strict posture, a deployment that declares no replay tier is refused at the
configuration boundary: it names no replay state, so no serving deployment is built over it.
For a deployment that reaches replay admission, admission refuses before any store side effect
when the declared tier is below the strict-production minimum or the wired store self-reports
the single-process reference class. The atomic admission is the LAST step, and a store that does not answer it refuses the exchange rather than
admitting it — reported as an outage, never as a replay.
corrections.old:
Under the fleet-strict posture, replay admission refuses before any store side effect when
the deployment declares no replay tier, declares one below the strict-production minimum, or
wires a store that self-reports the single-process reference class. The atomic admission is
the LAST step, and a store that does not answer it refuses the exchange rather than
admitting it — reported as an outage, never as a replay.

corrections.new:
The two gates it composes are of different kinds and the claim keeps them apart. The
DECLARED tier is the operator's statement: its absence is refused by the configuration owner,
`proxy.replay_configuration_state`, before a serving deployment exists, and a declared tier
below the strict-production minimum is refused by the admission owner,
`proxy.replay_admission_gate`. The store's self-reported durability class is the object's own,
checked beneath. A deployment can get the first right and the
second wrong, which is why both refuse, and why neither is called a check on the other.

reason: Owner ruling 2026-10-14 item 2 (option 1). Since MCPRE-166 (#1113) a fleet-strict deployment with no declared replay tier is unrepresentable at replay admission (`ReplayPosture::FleetStrict` carries its tier) and is refused at the configuration boundary by `proxy.replay_configuration_state` (`no_declared_tier_yields_no_state`). The statement named replay admission as the locus of that refusal. It now states the two stages: the configuration boundary refuses the undeclared tier before a serving deployment exists; replay admission still refuses the below-minimum tier and the single-process store class before any store side effect; an unanswered store is still an outage. The scope names the configuration owner and the admission owner. `unit://proxy.replay_configuration_state` joins `supported_by`. The security consequence, the dependencies and the Redis/etcd premise treatment are unchanged.
